**1 Timothy 1**

*Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, and Lord Jesus Christ, which is our hope;*

*2 Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.*

*3 As I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine,*

*4 Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: so do.*

*5 Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned:*

*6 From which some having swerved have turned aside unto vain jangling;*

*7 Desiring to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.*

*8 But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully;*

*9 Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,*

*10 For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine;*

*11 According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

*12 And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry;*

*13 Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.*

*14 And the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.*

*15 This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.*

*16 Howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might shew forth all longsuffering, for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting.*

*17 Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.*

*18 This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare;*

*19 Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck:*

*20 Of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.*

Today we begin the series called "the Pastoral Epistles," Paul's letters to Timothy and Titus, respectively, giving them doctrine on planting churches and the only two biblical church offices; Bishop and Deacon. Bishop being the pastor, or head of a local independent NT church, and decon being an assistive role, aiding the pastor in the administration of the church.

Here Paul writes to Timothy, his "son" in Christ, whom the last Apostle had won to the Lord, and who he is asking to remain in Ephesus, planting churches.

The doctrines he teaches are instrumental in how God wishes to see our local churches established and run. In their roles as evangelist, Timothy and Titus are instrumental in passing on this instruction to those called to the offices.

Most denominations ignore this teaching, entirely. The very notion of denomination, central control, unqualified priests, unbiblical hierarchies and the like, spreading bad doctrine by decree.

Even OIFB churches, who as Baptists recognize the two offices doctrine, have abandoned the traditional training of future pastors, evangelists and church planting and embraced the unbiblical Bible College racket, siphoning off potential men of God and other young people, to feed them into a collegiate system that does more to promote and spread heresy than anything else.

God's plan for churches is to train up future leaders, be pastor-led, and to go out soul winning, evangelizing a receptive community, and eventually planting a church and sending off a pastor, who then repeats the process.

Some pastors grew so far and fast, they took pride in establishment of their Christian schools and Bible colleges, and for many, it was their eventual downfall in their service to the Lord.

So, as we wade into the doctrines laid out here, we see that Timothy is charged with instructing those he finds called to the office of bishop, or pastor as we call it in modern times (terms that come from overseeing a flock of sheep), that they give no heed to fables and genealogies that lead to foolish questions, and don't edify the congregation. This is similarly given to Titus, avoiding Jewish fables and endless genealogies to instruct the future leaders of these churches.

At the time of this writing, many of the apocryphal books had been in circulation, non-inspired and many heretical concepts, being used by Jews and similarly creeping in to the new Christian churches.

The ramifications of rejecting the teachings of the pastoral epistles can still be felt today, with apostate false church of Rome, which uses unqualified men in unbiblical positions and uses the apocrypha, Jewish fables, to create doctrines. Not just the fables of the already existing books during Paul's day, such as using Maccabees to create the lie of purgatory,  but false gospels of Thomas and Andrew, for example, which they've adopted their Mary-worship from.

Of course we have the genealogies attempting to paint "seeds of Abraham" as special, continued in dispensationalist heresy today.

Paul continues to say that, in instruction of these leaders to also stress the importance of *charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.* The gracious love for others that comes from having a good conscience before God, being blameless and regenerate in the faith of Christ. Unfeigned, sincere. While all saved have reconciliation with God regarding their sin, it is a spiritual maturity that brings one to this gracious and merciful charitable love for others.

There are some, Paul informs us, that having neglected this trait, and professing themselves wise, have become fools. Vain jangling. Just pontificating on the matters of the law, and works, and neglecting the faith, and forgiveness and grace. Many such cases, even today.

Paul does caution that the law of God *is good,* in itself, for its purpose, which he lays out here. His admonition is against the legalistic works-based false teachers, not the law itself, which we who are saved have liberty from, but that the law continues to serve as a schoolmaster, and is *for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.* To bring them to the knowledge of the Gospel, or at the very least, to punish wrongdoing on earth and to keep an orderly society, understanding that the majority of people are not saved.

To many people, both believers and naturally, unbelievers, see no benefit or roles in God's law being used today. "That was for those times. Not for today." But, as we see from this list of sins, there is a clear need to maintain God's law regardless of what current year is.

Whoremongers and whores, who defile themselves with mankind, murderers, liars and every other thing that is contrary to good teaching from scripture. It's a broad list, and we understand why there remains a need to enforce these things.

There is an element of libertarian Christian that doesn't just reject the Levitical laws and carnal ordinances, done away with in Christ, but see no need to enforce the laws of God, written in our hearts and proclaimed from Adam on by God. They take their liberty for license to sin, and will not support the role of government and the law to protect people from evil and bring people to the understanding that there is sin and punishment, which is key to coming to repentance and accepting salvation.

But, those sincere in the faith and who understand the charity, the gracious love given by God to them, as sinners and able to show that love to others, are able and fit for the ministry. Paul uses himself as an example of this, that being a chief of sinners, who did evil against believers, was so changed by God and the gospel of reconciliation in Jesus, that has made him effective in the ministry he was appointed to, and the glory of God it has allowed him.

He encourages Timothy with this, and warns against those who, having been put away from the faith, who are reprobate, two of whom Paul names, infamous for their attempts to shipwreck, to lead to ruin, the faith of others. *Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.*

**1 Timothy 2**

*I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;*

*2 For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.*

*3 For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour;*

*4 Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.*

*5 For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;*

*6 Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.*

*7 Whereunto I am ordained a preacher, and an apostle, (I speak the truth in Christ, and lie not;) a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and verity.*

*8 I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.*

*9 In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;*

*10 But (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works.*

*11 Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.*

*12 But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.*

*13 For Adam was first formed, then Eve.*

*14 And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.*

*15 Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.*

Paul, having laid out his instruction to Timothy, and his role in establishment of churches of the Ephesians, and giving some basic commands in that regard, and a warning against reprobate false prophets, moves therefore to spell out a broader doctrine that applies to all Christians. It is how to develop the men to have the temperament that will produce those fit for the office and called to that ministry, and how to edify the church, bringing in more believers.

The first point, praying for all men, supplications, or asking of God for favor, thanksgiving for the blessings He bestows, intercessions that the Spirit may work to bring about outcomes that give glory to God.

This is our instruction for the rulers of this world as much as the beggars, that we may live peaceably. Not given to fear or wrath. This causes many to bristle, but as much as possible we are to live peaceably and without offense, with all men, so we may in all godliness and honesty, bring others to the truth.

*For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;*

We are to be a testimony to the truth of this. That our prayers and faith be lived out in a way that brings others to this truth. Doubt and wrath show a lack of faith and offends others from the truth. Simple as.

The spiralling people do when it comes to the cares of this world, or their fearful outbursts show a lack of faith in the same God who they are supposed to be magnifying and giving glory to, as witness to others.

Note that Jesus is our sole mediator for intercession with God. Not spirits of men. Not idols or preists. When we pray for others it is asking Jesus to intercede, God in His name to bless, the holy Spirit to give comfort.

Also, the Bible says the will of God our savior that ALL MEN come to believe. It isn't a select few as Calvinism would claim, and it is our calling to help make God's will manifest.

So men should be holy, in prayer, without fear, peaceable, without doubt and wrath. Praying for all men to come to the truth, even for the government that God may grant us peace, allowing more to be saved.

In a similar manner, women have a role as well. Just as men who are unruly and fearful offer a bad testimony so to do women who dress immodestly, who are ostentatious in their appearance. Not only because of the obvious temptations, but as speaking to their character as Godly women. The two admonitions, one for men and one for women, have the same root context. That we show outward signs of the faith that is saved us to better bring others to salvation.

It's often the men who are most fearful and wrathful, who have the loudest voice in pointing out to women not to dress shamefully. In this regard they are hypocrites. Women should do that which is pleasing to God, but so should men, we have an equal role in winning souls to Christ.

Wear those rolls differ, the Bible says women aren't to teach, because, like eve, they are prone to being deceived regarding God's word. This is just the truth of it, and it is a sentiment found throughout the Epistles, and borne out by experience. This is not to excuse Adam and condemn eve, but rather just clarifying rules and natural tendencies to better demonstrate God's will.

Paul goes on to say that it is in bearing children, and raising them up in a Godly way, that women have the greater influence than men leading the church. That they are saved, preserved and protected, by the generations of children that they bring into the world and give witness to God to, that they may be His.

Too many cherry pick these verses and create an artificial men versus women divide. It is about roles and responsibilities, understanding there are differences between men and women. And we have different deficiencies and negative tendencies that can trip us up in our walk with God.
But we should take comfort that when we follow God's will, we have the opportunity to bring Him glory just the same.

This is a rushed breakdown of the chapter, but I hope those with ears to hear understand my meaning. This is one of those difficult concepts God teaches us, that is full of nuance, and is far more balanced then people would believe. Especially the tendency of men who are derelict in their role, yet insistent women be dedicated in theirs. Also a lot of men are weak in the spirit and fearful in the flesh, and struggle with the idea that they too answer to a hierarchy, that exists for God's will. And in their impatience with God's longsuffering, and their fear which comes from lack of faith, their doubt which causes them to come to wrath rather than leaving it up to God, they are as a woman who is dressed like a harlot as far as their testimony is concerned. And while a woman should not be allowed to teach in a church, neither should a fearful and wrathful man.

**Isaiah 45**

*²¹Tell ye, and bring them near; yea, let them take counsel together: who hath declared this from ancient time? who hath told it from that time? have not I the Lord? and there is no God else beside me; a just God and a Saviour; there is none beside me.*

*²²Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else.*

*²³I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.*

**1 Timothy 3**

*This is a true saying, if a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.*

*2 A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach;*

*3 Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;*

*4 One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity;*

*5 (For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)*

*6 Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.*

*7 Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.*

*8 Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;*

*9 Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.*

*10 And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.*

*11 Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.*

*12 Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.*

*13 For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.*

*14 These things write I unto thee, hoping to come unto thee shortly:*

*15 But if I tarry long, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.*

*16 And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.*

Now, having laid a baseline for general behavior that should be encouraged in the newly planted churches, to better bring about the type of men to be trusted with keeping watch over the flock, Paul moves on to describe the basic qualities required for the two offices the Bible provides us; Bishop and Deacon.

Note these aren't preists, or a honorific for high preists, the way the false denominations use the term "bishop," as we know all saints are part of the royal preisthood of believers. Rather, this is specifically about pastors, leading the flock and deacons who help him minister.

If you recall, deacon was the position created by the Apostles at the churches in Jerusalem back in Acts 6:

*Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables. Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word. And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch: whom they set before the apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them. And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly;*

We see in this that the churches are to be led by those ministering the Gospel, and the day to day management left to the deacons who work for them.

Many modern churches are deacon-led, and this has caused innumerable problems, politicizing a church. They should be Christ-led, pastor in charge, deacons serving the pastor, as the Bible lays out.

And here we come to the qualifications for each office, and see they are basically the same. Married, to one wife. With orderly children and household. In all gravity, meaning he takes this first role as husband and father  seriously. Many churches have failed because their pastor, who may be a godly man, with a good wife and seemingly orderly house, allowed sin and disorder into their homes, which in turn affected the church, brining many to ruin.

Not this isn't saying he, his wife or kids must be perfect, but that the pastors and deacons be in control at home. This could mean a child act up, and being sufficiently punished, or even put out. Rather than their sins covered up and allowed due to the pastor or deacon's position. Many such cases.

Sober men. Not given to wine, but full of hospitality for others. Not greedy. Not a striker, not a brawler. Not greedy for filthy lucre, money earned by dishonest means, and selling of favor from his position. Not covetous. Not a novice, who may be filled with pride at his newfound position of power.

These are *men* who are established in the faith. We have already seen in the previous chapter that these offices cannot be for women, who aren't to be suffered to teach in the church. Female pastors are not biblical, and with reason.

But of the men, they should be *Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience...And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.*

We see what that mystery of faith is, the Gospel. Some have taken the first verse out of context to bring in gnostic heresy regarding some sort of oral tradition known only to those chosen to lead, but Paul gives the answer to the mystery. Their faith in Jesus as the redeemer, giving them a good conscience.

They must also have wives who are *grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things,* because in truth and practice, though the wife isn't holding the office, they find themselves with duties and responsibilities within the church.

These ideas regarding the two biblical offices of the local independent NT churches are further developed in the remaining pastoral epistles, but sufficient groundwork has been laid here to see what churches aren't using the scriptural standard, and so, reject them. In the next chapter, we will see further, Paul writing in the Spirit tells Timothy some warning signs of false teachers to watch out for.

*And God said, Let there be light: and there was light...*

*This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.*..

Then *spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life...*

That *was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.*..

*And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.*
*For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God...*

*Then Jesus said unto them, Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you: for he that walketh in darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.*

*While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them...*

*But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.*..

*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light...*

*For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.*..

*The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?*

*Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward.*

*And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever.*

**1 Timothy 4**

*Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils;*

*2 Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron;*

*3 Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.*

*4 For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving:*

*5 For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.*

*6 If thou put the brethren in remembrance of these things, thou shalt be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine, whereunto thou hast attained.*

*7 But refuse profane and old wives' fables, and exercise thyself rather unto godliness.*

*8 For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.*

*9 This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.*

*10 For therefore we both labour and suffer reproach, because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.*

*11 These things command and teach.*

*12 Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.*

*13 Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.*

*14 Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.*

*15 Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.*

*16 Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.*

Paul, expressly speaking in the Spirit, warns that in the latter times, the period post-ascension and before the day of the Lord's return, that some will depart from the faith, to teach doctrines of devils.

The Holy Spirit describes these false prophets as having their conscience seared, because they are reprobates, and so they speak lies and hypocrisy.

Again, this isn't Paul's spiritual discernment leading to his writing a prophetic dark saying, he says this is directly spoken by the Spirit, by God. And these are the examples of what those devilish doctrines of lies will teach; Forbidding to marry and abstaining from meats, insinuating that they will deceive those giving heed to seducing spirits, with the appearance of holiness.

It shouldn't have to be said that this is directed at the same heresies the RCC would eventually take up. Their doctrines of devils.

This is one of many admonitions against specific practices that the Catholic Church and many of its harlot daughters teach. Warnings against Idolatry, building ornate temples, vain repetitive prayers, having other mediators with God the Father than the man Christ Jesus, calling men "Father," taking heed to Jewish fables, adding works and "sacraments" to the Gospel, disregarding God's word as the only source for doctrine, persecution of believers, and here, forbidding to marry and abstaining from meats.

As if that were not enough, there is Scripture recording Jesus saying to those seeking to worship Mary, "*Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it*." and "*Who is my mother, or my brethren?...Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother."*

The word of God, spoken before the foundation of the world, and published in these latter times, expressly addresses the false teachers and their doctrines of what Jesus' revelation to John calls "the whore of Babylon." More than 200 years before the Roman empire created the Catholic Church. And still today some take heed of its seducing spirits and are led astray.

Now to edify Timothy in his role as evangelist to the Ephesians, Paul gives yet more advice as to the doctrines he should be certain to instruct the churches.

That every creature is good to eat, *For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer*, just as God told Adam and again to Noah. The dietary laws and carnal ordinances given to Moses for a season, done away with in Christ. This understanding will help the men of the church "be a good minister of Jesus Christ," not because of the food they eat, but rather the understanding of prayer and God's blessing. That, as Jesus said, *the flesh profits nothing,* rather they will *be  nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine.*

And so, avoid old wives tales, similarly, Jewish fables, and be about exercising godliness, their spirit, not the flesh.

*For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.*

We the saved, *having*, present tense, the promise of the life that now is and the eternal life that awaits, must exercise and grow, spiritually. Godliness is our gainz, for our eternal life will be built upon that, not our PRs at the gym.

*This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.*

And therefore, because of this doctrine of faith, living Godly, in the spiritual rather than the flesh, the *faithful sayings* Paul writes unto Timothy, he warns they will both labor to teach others, and be rebuked by those of this world, *because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.*

(Note to calvinists, God is the savior of all men, specially those who believe. Christ died for everyone, especially to those who believe and are saved)

The chapter wraps up with more encouragement for Timothy from Paul, to *give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.* To not let his youth be a hindrance to his ordained role, but to meditate and study these doctrines and live an example that, being blameless, will inspire others to see past his being young, because he is strong in the faith. Reminding him he has the Holy Ghost upon him, and to rely on that to bring the newly formed churches around.

**1 Timothy 5**

*Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren;*

*2 The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity.*

*3 Honour widows that are widows indeed.*

*4 But if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God.*

*5 Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.*

*6 But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.*

*7 And these things give in charge, that they may be blameless.*

*8 But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.*

*9 Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man.*

*10 Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.*

*11 But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry;*

*12 Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.*

*13 And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.*

*14 I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.*

*15 For some are already turned aside after Satan.*

*16 If any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.*

*17 Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.*

*18 For the scripture saith, thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.*

*19 Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.*

*20 Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.*

*21 I charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.*

*22 Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure.*

*23 Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities.*

*24 Some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after.*

*25 Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.*

*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world*.
...
*Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.*
...
*He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.*

There are two groups of people God has a special place for, and asks us to be protectors and caretakers of; widows and orphans.

This biblical appeal actually became a means by which many fraternal orders, Masonic lodges and other less than godly organizations worked a grift. Collecting donations for the "widows and orphans fund" became a euphemism for this kind of shakedown charity by the 20th Century. The idea itself synonymous with corruption. A punchline euphemism for illegal activities hidden under the guise of charity.

But in more recent decades, the concept, both Biblical and corrupt has all but disappeared, as the state welfare and entitlements has supplanted it. Now hardly any one, and sadly, few churches, give heed to the "pure religion" God commands us towards.

Here, in chapter 5 of first Timothy, Paul instructs the young evangelist on the proper church role and management for care of widows indeed.

Before getting to that, and continuing the thought of chapter 4 regarding Timothy's youth, and how to minimize those who look down on being told what to do by a younger man, Paul gives instruction. Don't rebuke an elder. Treat them as fathers, younger men as brothers, young girls as sisters (with a purity), and elderly women as mothers. This applies to us all, and our fellow congregants. We are family for Christ's sake, and as such have obligation for respect, and at times, honor.

Honor in the Bible has a financial aspect to it, that we give honor, payment, support, to our parents, is one of the main meanings behind the commandment. Giving honor to whom it is due is a point repeatedly made by God throughout the Bible, and this is the context of Paul's instructions here.

A widow indeed is one who, having lost her husband and not having sons or nephews (which means not only her siblings' children but grandchildren, and other younger relations), that these family members must honor her with support, that she not be a burden to the church. He warns;

*But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.*

This is similar language to those facing church discipline laid out by Jesus, that they be put out from the congregation and treated as if they are unsaved. Heathens. Infidels.

As a side note, that may help with understanding these passages; just as "saved" in scripture isn't always referring to justification by faith, but often physical salvation from danger, "faith" isn't always referring to the saving faith that we need to be redeemed. Often, especially in the epistles (which are written to believers), "faith" can refer to the deeper trust in God, or being faithful to His commands and expectations, or our own responsibility to others. And in the same manner, "condemnation," "damnation," "justified,"  or even "infidel" may be being applied in the present sense, regarding how one is looked at by others, not their spiritual condition in regards to eternal life. These are important distinctions, and understanding the context of the terms when they are used will save you when some try to cherry pick verses to come to a different meaning regarding salvation.

Continuing, Paul lists more qualifiers for a widow "indeed," that she be desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day. Poor, no means of support and giving her life to the faith, essentially. Further, he goes on to say she must be over 60, blameless and devoted to ministry of the church, and the wife of one man;

..*having been the wife of one man. Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.*

This makes her a true widow. A widow indeed.

Paul contrasts this with the exceptions. One who lives for pleasure rather than service is excluded, for example. And age is a factor;

*The younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith. And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.*

Young women, who could still remarry, shouldn't be given the honor by the church. Even if they swear they will be devoted to the ministry, and continuing in prayer, etc, Paul says they eventually will become wonton, that is, spoiled and pampered, having financial support with little to do all day but gossip and carry on, it will corrupt them, and eventually they will seek out a man to remarry, and make them abandon their first faith, that is that God will provide for them through the church that they are swearing devotion to, and leave for a husband. Damnation in this context means condemned by others for her behavior, not losing her salvation or going to Hell.

This is all true, we witness it ourselves today, especially with welfare taking the place of charity or family support. And frequently you may see at church a godly woman, coming from divorce or a husband's death, will put herself all in to helping out to keep herself busy, and eventually get married, often to an unsaved man, or worse, a man of the church she led to adultery and divorce, and her testimony becomes an open shame. Many such cases.

We see though out 1 Timothy, and other epistles but especially here, that the testimony to the unsaved by living blamelessly so that they may reach the lost with soul winning, is a top priority.

That they *give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.*

Shifting gears, Paul gets back to how to handle elders of the church;

*Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine. For the scripture saith, thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.*

*Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.*
*Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.*

So elders that serve the congregation faithfully should receive double honor, double payment for their efforts. Rewarded financially for their time.

And accusations against them should be handled with respect, the same manner of which Jesus laid out, requiring witnesses and reproached privately, but publicly shamed and cast out if they don't repent.

Far too many churches only do the first half, and then often will defer to the elder and their profession of innocence. It is sadly rare that they be openly shamed and cast out for their indiscretions and sin. Especially sexual immorality. The topic can be embarrassing for all involved, and the older man's excuses taken with more veracity than the younger girls (or boys) accusations. There is often fear of the entire congregation being smeared, and excuses and rationalizations made. This is the downfall to many churches, especially those that have drifted from biblical fundamentalism, and grown lukewarm.

By not being respecters of persons in these matters, and worrying less about our own appearances, and more about doing what's right, an active lively church can avoid these pitfalls.

If your church has an elder or any member, for that matter, who engages in sinful activities, especially fornication, adultery, and taking advantage of their position against young ones, they need to be put out, and put out publicly, and police involved if necessary.

There is no excuse. Jesus will remove the candlestick of a church that does this. The hedge of protection will be gone.

Paul charges these things to Timothy before God. This is a command as to how he should behave and what he must teach to the churches he is planting. It's a sacred duty. We have the same duty to our own churches, to maintain these standards and practices. To exercise pure religion, undefiled.

He orders Timothy to not lay hands suddenly on no man. This may be an admonition against brawling, but more likely in this context, he means ordination with the Holy Ghost.

Not to partake in another man's sin, which is great advice to us all.

He says before you judge remember that while some good works or wrong doings may seem obvious, others come out later so basically don't make snap judgments.

The kindly medical advice, to drink wine, (obviously meaning juice here as booze isn't good for the stomach), seems a non sequitur in the midst of being instructed not to show favoritism and be patient and reserved in judgment, but it seems apropos given the stress of the position and the weight of what's been charged to the young church planter.

**1 Timothy 6**

*Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.*

*2 And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort.*

*3 If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness;*

*4 He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,*

*5 Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.*

*6 But godliness with contentment is great gain.*

*7 For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.*

*8 And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.*

*9 But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.*

*10 For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.*

*11 But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.*

*12 Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.*

*13 I give thee charge in the sight of God, who quickeneth all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession;*

*14 That thou keep this commandment without spot, unrebukable, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:*

*15 Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;*

*16 Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.*

*17 Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;*

*18 That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate;*

*19 Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on eternal life.*

*20 O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called:*

*21 Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen.*

The final chapter in 1st Timothy, and it is building on the theme of being able to give a good testimony for Christ to others by living like you have the gift of eternal life, not stuck in the cares of this world but growing in spirit.

The admonition to obey earthly authority, to please God and make His glory seen of man that you may give a good witness is repeated throughout the New Testament, from Jesus rendering unto Caesar, to Romans 13 and 1 Peter 2, and elsewhere. This is one of the hardest doctrines for most American Christians today, spoiled by the supposed promises of "Liberty" from the Constitution, and missing the liberty we have in Christ.

We bristle with pride at the idea of being good servants at work, living agreeably with all men as much as possible, paying taxes, tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom. Honor to parents and elders. This doctrine is seen as being a "Christ cuck." Seen as weak by those lacking understanding. Missing that while we defer to authority, we have roles of authority in God's hierarchy ourselves, and that we are instructed to always place God and His word as our final authority.

Often those who cry loudest about supposed persecution and calls for riot and seditions, have abandoned their own roles, or are derelict in their own responsibilities. They care more for their comfort than for their testimony. They live in fear rather than faith. They see wrath as theirs, not God's.

They, not being satisfied with what God has given them, and impatient with His longsuffering, are unable to bring others to believe and so, shoot themselves in the foot and worsen their own condition.

We have one means to lead a nation back from wickedness, and that is the Gospel. Soul winning. Revival. And that requires our being good witnesses to the power of the Spirit and faith that God, who is holy and just, and will keep His promise and restore us.

Paul is writing to Timothy who, living in Macedonia, a slave/caste society, will have gotten both masters and slaves saved, and in the same congregation. We are blessed not to be living in a society that openly enslaves people. But the same admonition applies to us as wage-slaves.

Be the best employee at your job. Even if your boss is terrible. Your employer, even if he despises religion and doesn't know Christ should still be forced by your witness to see Christians as good employees. The best, because we work for God not them. Those of us *under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.*

We represent Christ to the world. We are to be a light that draws men near.

And again, this isn't to say if a manager calls on you to do something that is contrary to God's word that you have to submit. We defer to the higher authority and there is none higher than God. But we do it peaceably, and with humility and meekness, trusting in God to save us should it lead to persecution.

We don't obey to avoid being persecuted, but to please God, and with the full expectation that we might face tribulation when we defer to God's will over earthly authority.

Paul uses Jesus' own example before Pilate, which by His meek silence led to Pilate confessing He was blameless, and leading to the Glory of God in the crucifixion.

*But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.*

Opposition to this doctrine often amounts to the same general notion as a black shooting another black for "dissing" them by stepping on they Jordans.

It's the same foolish pride, wrathful anger, and covetous materialism. Not a witness of someone who has the power of the Holy Spirit indwelling them.

And if a false teacher says otherwise? If they teach rebellion, wrath and riot?

*He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings, Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.*

Christianity is not a sovereign citizen movement. The liberty we have in Christ is true liberty, from sin and Hell and death. Made heirs to the Kingdom. We have eternal life in Him and the life we have on this world is short. The rewards we seek for eternity have a short time to be earned. The more we waste on petty, temporal things, the more we shortchange God and ourselves.

Paul continues, spinning off the warning about staying away from those who see earthly gain as proof of godliness, seeking after riches, we are given the adage "the love of money is the root of all evil." Storing up treasure on earth leads to temptations and snares, traps of our own making. Seeking after wealth while neglecting our stores in Heaven.

*O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.*

Be satisfied with what God blessed you with, even if it is subsistence, knowing that if you win souls, your riches in Heaven will be greater.

*Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.*

This is our calling, as those who have laid hold on eternal life; to live as though we believe it. That our hope isn't in vain, but on the promises of God, faithful and true.

The promise that as we live blamelessly, *unrebukable,* that when Christ returns for the Day of the Lord, everyone will get as they gave, and justice will be served. God's wrath upon those who have troubled us. Vengeance being His.

*Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;*
*Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.*

Finishing up, Paul advises that Timothy lay charge to those who are converted to the faith and already rich in wealth to be ready to hand it out to those in need. To do good works with that they've been blessed. To despise their riches here and store up rewards for Heaven.

As Jesus told His disciples, it is harder for a rich man to enter the Kingdom than for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle. And because to whom much is given, much more is expected, they should be encouraged to do as much as possible for the brethren, edifying the church and giving glory to God.

Finally, Paul warns young Timothy, his son in Christ, a ward of the Gospel, to

*Keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith.*

We are entrusted with the Gospel of reconciliation. The doctrines of how to live, discipleship, prudence, fidelity to God's law and hope in His promise. To preach and to teach this to every creature. Saving who we can, by mercy or by warning of the fire.

We should give good witness to this faith that we have been entrusted, the surety of which is our now quickened spirit, and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit inside us. A ready and meek answer for our hope to all who we give witness.

We are to avoid the vain, that is unprofitable babblings of those seeking to debate us, to engender strife and disputations of the faith. Not to give answer to fools. Not to get into arguments with gnostics, and their science, falsely so-called. This includes debating atheists on creation, for example. We are warned repeatedly against answering a fool in their folly.

*8 Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.*

*9 Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning.*

It is a bad witness to get caught up in disputations with a heretic. (Of this, I am chief)

**Titus 3:10-11**
*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.*

(This is primarily the reason for my pinned rules for the channel. To keep myself from sinning, being drawn into debates with fools. It's also why Twitter is such a snare.)

The meat of the word, giving us instruction on how we should carry ourselves as saved Christians, to be a good witness, to live faith to faith, growing in the spirit, studying to be approved unto God, understanding the liberty we have in Christ, what the implications are for those of us possessing eternal life, what to expect at Jesus' coming, God's plan and promise, His justice and wrath...all this is impossible to understand without first understanding salvation in Christ. Without which you cannot receive even the milk of the word, as born again babes.

The light of the Lord shines on us for a brief time, the Spirit convicts and draws the unbelieving to the light for a limited time, and then if a person remains unreceptive, is hid away. God gives every opportunity to you to repent and believe on Jesus Christ for salvation, but it isn't limitless.

*To day if ye will hear his voice,*
*Harden not your heart...behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation...Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near!*

Just as God was longsuffering to the unbelieving as Noah built his ark, and then shut the door, too late to be saved, so to is His offer of grace.

*While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.*

If you have not believed on Jesus Christ as the ONLY means of forgiveness and righteousness, if you have not accepted God's free gift of salvation, if you have been being called to the wedding feast, but have made excuse not to accept, or are trying to work your way in, repent.

Tomorrow is not promised. You are being called today. Don't wait until it is too late. Don't harden your heart.
